source.title: Critical Learning Periods in Deep Neural Networks
source.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR); arXiv:1711.08856

confidence_rationale: Highest-mapping-fidelity source: an ARTIFICIAL neural network (same abstract class as the REE substrate, no biochemistry) in which a deficit applied during an early developmental window causes IRREVERSIBLE loss, while the identical deficit applied later is fully recoverable. That is exactly Q-088's dissociation between develop-without-the-mechanism and mature-state manipulation, demonstrated in a computational learning system. Downgraded from higher because the substrate is a vision CNN, not an RL/world-model agent, and the paper does not report the exact numeric magnitudes in the abstract.
failure_signatures: Deficits that do not perturb low-level input statistics (e.g. vertical image flip) leave NO lasting mark and are fully overcome by further training -- i.e. not every developmental perturbation dissociates, so a null dissociation in REE would not by itself falsify the substrate; it may mean the lesioned mechanism does not shape the plastic early phase.

The dissociation magnitude depends on network size and on deficit onset/length -- a REE probe run at the wrong developmental timing, or on a substrate too small to show information-plasticity collapse, could report AGREE for reasons unrelated to the mechanism's developmental necessity.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In deep networks, a temporary stimulus deficit during an early critical window permanently impairs skill acquisition (mimicking animal critical-period data), whereas the same deficit later is recoverable; the effect tracks a rise-then-fall of Fisher-Information 'Information Plasticity' and arises from learning dynamics alone, not biochemistry.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-088 asks whether developing a REE agent WITHOUT a developmentally-necessary mechanism (competitive redevelopment) gives a different verdict than removing it after maturity (mature-state lesion). Achille et al. is direct computational evidence that early-phase perturbation and late-phase perturbation of a learning system dissociate -- and, crucially, that this dissociation can emerge in a purely artificial substrate from information-processing constraints. This raises the prior that REE's develop-without protocol will disagree with mature lesion, i.e. that the expensive protocol buys real information.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The result establishes that computational learning systems CAN show develop-vs-mature dissociation, not that REE's specific INV-055 infant-stage mechanism does. Whether the REE substrate exhibits an analogous information-plasticity collapse is precisely the open question -- this paper supplies a strong prior, not a substitute for the probe. The measured system is supervised vision CNN training; REE is a reinforcement/world-model agent, and the shape of its plastic window is unmeasured.
mapping.source_context: Supervised image-classification CNNs (CIFAR/ImageNet-style), cataract-like blur and other deficits imposed over training-epoch windows; Fisher-Information analysis of weights.

confidence_components.notes: Foundational, heavily-cited ICLR paper; the computational-to-computational transfer keeps transfer_risk low relative to the biological analogs, but domain (vision CNN vs RL agent) caps mapping_fidelity below 0.8.
